3. Sheikh Liakat Ali and two others tiled Writ Petition No.333 of 1993 in the High Court Division challenging the orders passed in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 and taking over possession of the land and the structure of holding No.14/1, Topkhana Road, Dhaka stating that they are the owners of the "Usree" house and the land measuring an area of .4925 acre of khas mohal plot No. 188, ward No.3, Sheet No.20, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as "disputed property"). The disputed property originally belonged to the Collectorate of Dhaka who settled the same to Satyendra Nath Roy (S.N.Roy), Professor of the University of Dhaka on 08.12.1937 for a period of 23 years 3 months by a registered deed of lease. Satyendra Nath Roy constructed two storied building thereon and named the same as "Usree". He gifted the disputed property to his wife Sreemoti Sujata Roy by registered deed dated 18.05.1940. The Government requisitioned the said building on 23.09.1947 and paid rent to Sujata Roy. Sujata Roy transferred the said property to Munshi Ashraf Ali, predecessor-in-interest of the writ petitioner-respondents by a registered sale deed dated 26.03.1951. Said Ashraf Ali got the order of lease extended by registered deed of lease dated 07.08.1961. Ashraf Ali submitted several representations to the Government to get the said property released from the order of requisition. Thus, the Government de-requisitioned the said "Usree" house on 09.07.1971. He let out the said house to Bangladesh National Awami Party (NAP). After creation of BAKSAL in January 1975, NAP was merged with BAKSAL. NAP left the disputed house in May 1975. Ashraf Ali went to ascertain the position of the disputed property and found that the police locked up the house and posted police force for its security. On inquiry, he came to know that the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka had taken over possession of the said house. Ashraf Ali went to the office of the Deputy Commissioner and he was informed that the disputed property had been acquired by the Government in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 for construction of the building of Press Club. No notice for acquisition was ever served upon Ashraf Ali. He submitted several representations to the Government to get the said property released from acquisition. Ashraf All died on 18.03.1976 and his wife died on 05.04.1992. Thereafter, his heirs the petitioners made similar representations that notice of acquisition was served upon the owner of the disputed property and that the building of the Press Club was constructed elsewhere so they are entitled to get the disputed property released. Meanwhile, the possession of the disputed property was taken over by the Government Accommodation Directorate, Ministry of Works and the Ministry of Works let out the same to the National Security Intelligence Department (NSI) on 27.08.1976. In such circumstances, the writ petitioner-respondents filed the instant writ petition and obtained Rule. 

 4. The High Court Division, by its judgment and order dated 17th June, 1996, made the said Rule absolute holding that (i) no gazette notification as to the decision of acquisition under section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 was published; (ii) allotment of the disputed property to the National Security Intelligence was illegal and unauthorised and (iii) the possession of the Government was also illegal. 

 7. The defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filing written statement and additional written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is barred by the provision of res-judicata and the same was not maintainable. The Government leased out disputed property to Professor Satyendra Nath Roy by a registered lease deed dated 31.11.1937 for a period of 23 years and 5 months. The said lessee constructed a two storied building thereon and named the same as "Uusree" house. He gifted the said property to his wile Sujata Roy by a registered deed dated 18.05.1940. Sujata Roy sold the disputed property to Munshi Ashraf Ali by a registered kabala dated 26.03. 1951. The Government renewed the original lease by a registered lease deed dated 07.08.1961 extending the period of lease for another 30 years with effect from 01.04.1961 to 31.03.1991. On the prayer of the Munshi Ashraf Ali, the Government de-requisitioned the suit property on 09.07.1971. After independence of Bangladesh. lessee Munshi Ashraf Ali let out the disputed property to Bangladesh National Awami Party (NAP). After formation of BAKSAL in the year 1975, the tenant (NAP) vacated the house in the month May, 1976 without giving any intimation to the landlord Munshi Ashraf Ali. Though the Government started L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 to acquire the disputed property for construction of the building of National Press Club which was not ultimately constructed. Meanwhile, the Director, Government Accommodation Directorate, claiming ownership of the disputed property, allotted the same for accommodation of the Office of N.S.I. When the defendants tried to get the disputed property released, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka recommended for release of the same as it was not required for the Press Club vide his letter dated 07.03.1985. But the N.S.I. denied to vacate the suit property. Thus, the defendants filed Writ Petition No.333 of 1993 and obtained Rule which was made absolute. The High Court Division declared the alleged acquisition illegal and void with a direction to the concerned authority to hand over possession of the disputed property to the defendants within 60 days and also to pay compensation for unauthorised occupation of the house. The leave petition against the said judgment dated 17.06.1996 was dismissed by the Appellate Division. The Government was compelled to hand over physical possession of the disputed property to these defendants. According to them their lease hold right had not been extinguished after 31.03.1991 since the same became permanent lease. 

 9. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney General appearing for the petitioner in Civil Review Petition No.334 of 2019, submits that the disputed property was acquired by the Government after due service of notice upon its lessee, that is, Munshi Ashraf Ali, predecessor-in-interest of the respondents of this review petition and the appellants of the Civil Appeal. He further submits that though the decision of acquisition was not notified in the official gazette, notices were duly served upon Munshi Ashraf Ali. After assessment of compensation, notice was issued upon him requesting to accept compensation but he did not turn up. Possession of the said property was duly taken over by the Government and same was handed over to the National Security Intelligence since Press Club, for which, the disputed property was acquired, was established elsewhere. He submits that though the disputed property was acquired for the Press Club, there is no legal bar for utilization of the same for another purpose. He submits that since notice of acquisition was duly served upon Munshi Ashraf Ali and the Government took over possession of the same and compensation was duly assessed and Munshi Ashraf Ali was duly notified to receive the compensation money, the right, title, interest and possession of the disputed land has been vested in the Government, the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the acquisition was illegal and the Government is unlawful possessor of the disputed land, this Division also committed error of law apparent on the face of the record in dismissing the civil petition. 

 14. Admittedly, the disputed property originally belonged to the Government. Case of the writ petitioner-respondents is that the Government settled the same to Professor Sattyandra Nath Roy on 30.11.1937 for a period of 23 years 3 months with effect from 01.01.1938 by registered deed of lease. S.N. Roy gifted his leasehold right to his wife Sujata Roy by registered deed of gift dated 18.05.1940. Sujata Roy sold the said property to Munshi Ashraf Ali, the predecessor-in-interest of the writ petitioner respondents. Ashraf Ali got his lease renewed on 07.08.1961 for a period of 30 years with effect from 01.04.1961. It is not disputed that the Government requisitioned the said property on 03.09.1947, that is, before the aforesaid transfer of Sujata Roy to Munshi Ashraf Ali. The further case of writ petitioners is that though the Government derequisitioned the disputed property on 17.09.1971 it did not handover the possession of the same to Munshi Ashraf Ali. He came to know that disputed property has been again requisitioned and, then, acquired in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70. Ashraf Ali made several representations to the Government to get the disputed property released from acquisition but the Government did not pay any heed. Rather, the Directorate of Government Accommodation, Ministry of Works illegally allotted the same to the National Security Intelligence Department (NSI). 

 15. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that the case record of L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 was called for by the High Court Division at the time of hearing of the writ petition and the High Court Division perused the same. The High Court Division held that the L.A. case was started on 07.07.1971 for acquisition but no notice in that regard was served upon the writ petitioner respondents. At the time of hearing of this review petition, learned Attorney General produced the case record of L.A. Case No.27/1969-70 for our perusal. We have also perused the record of the said L.A. case thoroughly. On perusal of the same, it appears that some papers from the said L.A. case are missing from the record. From the note sheet of L.A. Case it appears that on 07.07.1971, it was stated that "USREE" house was requisitioned immediately after partition on 23.09.1947 for the residential accommodation of the Government officials. Since then the disputed property was under the administrative control of the Estate Office, Dhaka. Subsequently, the Government decided to acquire the disputed property for the accommodation of Press Club. Accordingly, proposal for acquisition was made on 09.07.1971. For the said purpose of acquisition, it became necessary to derequisition of the disputed property. It further appears from the order dated 10.07.1971 of the L.A. Case No.27 of 69-70 that notice for derequisition was prepared for releasing the disputed property. The orders dated 07.07.1971 and 10.07.1971 in L.A. Case No.27 of 196970 were as follows: 

 The premises No. 14/3 Topkhana Road, Dacca known as USREE was requisitioned immediately after partition on 23.09.1947 for Residential accommodation. Since then the premises was under the administrative control of Estate office Dacca. Subsequently Govt. decided to acquire the land and building for the accommodation of the Press Club. Accordingly a proposal for requisition and acquisition of the holding was sought for on 09.07.1971 while it is necessary to derequisition the holding first & then to issue requisition notice with a view to acquire on urgent next basis. Kgo will please put up derequisition notice." 

 16. Accordingly, the Land Acquisition Officer issued notice releasing the disputed property from requisition with effect from 02.06.1971. Contents of the said notice run as follows: 

 18. Thereafter, the Land Acquisition Officer on 19.07.1971 passed the following order: 

 "3 19-7-71 Whereas in my opinion it is expedient and necessary in the public interest to requisition and acquisition this immoveable property described in the schedule below for requisition & acquisition of the land for accommodation of the E.P. Press Club. 

 19. It further appears from the record of L.A. case that notice was issued on 19.07.1971 to Ashraf Ali of No.68, Purana Paltan, P.S. Ramna, Dhaka and same was served on 20.07.1971. Date of service return was on 21.07.1971. In view of the provision of section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 official acts are presumed to have been rightly and regularly done. The maxim, "omnia prae-sumuntur rite esse acta" applied to official acts. Where any official act is shown to have been done in a manner substantially regular, it is presumed that formal requisites for its validity were complied with. It is curious that the writ petitioner-respondents though admitted the service of notices issued pursuant to the orders dated 07.07.1971 and 10.07.1971 but denied the notices issued pursuant to the subsequent orders dated 19.07.1971, 20.07.1971, 22.07.1971 and 26.07.1971. The High Court Division in its judgment failed to take notice of writ petitioners' double standard in respect of procedural validity of the same L.A. Case. Moreover, notices of the requisition and acquisition of the disputed property were served upon Ashraf Ali or not is a disputed question of fact which is difficult to ascertain in writ jurisdiction. 

 "6 26-7-71 Whereas 1 consider that the acquisition of the property described in the schedule below which were requisitioned by an order dated 22.07.71 under section 3 of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (Act XIII of 1948) is expedient for the purpose of East Pakistan Press Club. Notices are hereby given under sub-Section 1(a) & 3 read with Sub-Section 2 of section 5 of the said Act that the said properties are proposed to be acquired. 

 23. All persons interested in the properties are hereby called upon to appear before the A/L.A.O. or by an agent on the 19.08.71 at the office of the L.A.O. Dacca at 10 A.M. to state the nature of such interest in the properties objection if any to the acquisition of the property and particulars of their claims to compensation for their respective interest. 

 Certificate that I have this day the 22-7-1971 received possession from Mr. Md. Matiur Rahman, Add. Land Acquisition Officer, Dacca, for an area of more or less .48 acre of land in Mouza Shahar Dacca, Sheet No.20, Ward No.3, P.S. Ramna, Dist. Dacca, JL No.343, as per schedule/ below which has been requisitioned under section 3 of E.B. (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, XIII of 1948. 

 26. From the mote sheet of the L.A. case it appears that after the order dated 26.07.1971, rest portions of the note sheet of the L.A Case are missing. However, it further appears from the record that there is a letter issued from the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, Land Acquisition Department to the Section Officer, Ministry of Works and Urban Department, Public Works Division, Dhaka that notice under section 5(1 a) and 5(3) of the (Emergency) Requisition Act, 1948 was duly served upon the interested parties fixing the date 19.08.1971 for filing objection, if any, and actual possession of the land, building was delivered to the Sub-Divisional Engineer. Ramna (Bids) Division. The contents of the said letter dated 11.07.1974 run as follow: 

 "OFFICE OF THE DEPTUY COMMISSIONER, DACCA. LAND ACQUISITION DEPT. 

 Sub: Acquisition of land and building named "USREE" at 14/3, Topkhana Road Dacca for accommodation of Press Club. LA. Case No.27/69-70. 

 It appears from the case record that the premises No.14/3, Topkhana Road, Dacca known as "Usree" was requisitioned immediately after partition in the year 1947 for residential accommodation. Since then the premises was under the administrative control of the Estate Officer Dacca. Subsequently Govt. decided to acquire the land and buildings for accommodation of the Press Club. Accordingly the above premises was de-requisitioned by an order dated 10.07.1971 and requisitioned the land and building of the premises No.14/1 Topkhana Road afresh by an order dated 19.7.71 with a view to permanent acquisition for accommodation of the Press Club. The owner of the premises was offered advance payment but he did not receive the same. Physical possession of the land and building was delivered by Sub Divisional Engineer, Ramna (Bids), Division Dacca on 22.7.71 after making joint inventory. It is not known to this office how National Awami Party occupied the requisitioned property. 

 Notice u/s 5(la) and 5(3) for acquisition of the land was duly served upon the interested parties fixing 19.08.1971 for filing objections if any against the acquisition of the property but no objection against the acquisition of the property was received. Notice of acquisition has not yet been to the Govt. for publication in the official Gazette. 

 Sub: Acquisition of the house "USREE" at 14/3, Topkhana Road, Dacca for accommodation of E.P. Press Club (L.A. Case No.27/69-70). 

 Total Ruppes two fats eighteen thousand two hundred forty six only Certified that the estimate is fair and at the rates have been arrived at atter local enquiry and inspection of the ground and with reference to the settlement records and road Cess papers and the records of the Registration Department. Sd/- M.A. Kim, Sd/- Hossain Ali, Sd/- M.A. Hssain Land Acquisition Officer L.A.E A.D.C. (Rev), Dacca 

 33. From the record it further appears that the respondent No.1 Sk. Liakat Ali, admitting the fact of acquisition, prayed for release of the disputed property by filing an application addressing the ADC (L.A) Dhaka on 18.11.1984. In that application he, inter alia, stated, "To our utter surprise and dismay, the above holding was subsequently acquired in L.A case No.27 of 1969-70 for construction of Press Club, but the press club subsequently was constructed on a different site/the present site (where it stands now). Thus, the above holding was not used for the purpose for which it was acquired and no compensation was paid to the owner and as such no steps were taken to complete the acquisition proceedings." 

 34. The disputed property was allotted to the National Security Intelligence (N.S.I) who has been possessing the same repairing structures therein expending huge amount. The High Court Division though called for the record of L.A. Case No.27/1969-70, but without perusing the same meticulously and without taking into consideration of the facts and consequences of subsequent requisition and acquisition most abruptly drew conclusion that the Government is unauthorized possessor of the disputed property as it possessed the same forcibly which was erroneous and contrary to the provisions of law, this Division while deposing of the civil petition also failed to notice the same. 

 35. Section 3 of the Act provides the pro-vision that when a property is required permanently for a public purpose or in public interest, the Deputy Commissioner may requisition it with a view to its permanent acquisition for such public purpose or in such public interest. From Order No.3 dated 19.07.1971 it appears that the said provision was duly complied with. From the said order it was directed to Nazir to serve notice which was made in view of the provision provided in section 4 of the Act. Order 6 dated 26.07.1971 it is clear that all the steps under section 5 were complied with except publication of notification under section 5(7) of the Act. 

 36. It is true that the disputed property was acquired for construction of the building of Press Club but the Press Club was established elsewhere. It is also true that the notice under Section 5(7) (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 was not published in official gazette. Since the notices under Section 5(1a) and 5(3) were duly issued and served upon Munshi Ashraf Ali and provisional compensation for acquisition of disputed property was duly assessed and issuing notices, the Acquiring Authority requested the owner to receive the compensation and actual physical possession was taken over by the government, the right, title and possession of the disputed property has been vested in the Government. The writ petitioner respondents claimed that they are entitled to get back the possession of the disputed property since it has not been used for the purpose, for which, it was acquired but the said submission is not acceptable. 

 37. In the case of Brahmanbaria Pourasava Vs. Govt. of Bangladesh reported in 51 DIAZ (AD) 81 it has been held: " Again there is no principle of law under which once a property has been validly acquired for a public purpose, as admitted by the Government and has vested in the requiring body then even if the said property be utilised for a different purpose, the acquisition shall not stand void. A simple reading of section 8B of the Act shows that it does not come into operation in this circumstances of the case. So the order of withdrawal from acquisition in question cannot be sustained." 

 39. It appears that Munshi Ashraf Ali, the predecessor-in-interest of the writ petitioner respondents managed to get an exparte decree in Title Suit No.307 of 1975 in which it was declared that the disputed land was not requisitioned property and defendants of the said suit was permanently restrained for entering the disputed land but from the papers of L.A. Case No.27/1969-70 it appears that once disputed property was requisitioned and, then derequisitioned and thereafter, the same was acquired in L.A. Case No.27/1969-70. It further appears in the said suit that acquisition of the said property in afore-said L.A. Case was not challenged. Moreover, section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act provides the provision that no Civil Court shall entertain any suit against any order passed or action taken under the said Act. 

 41. On perusal of the notings in the note sheet of L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70, documents and other materials available in the record, it appears to us that there was no procedural irregularity or illegality in the process of acquisition of the disputed property. Only step was left that was the order of acquisition was not published in official gazette. That was the business of acquiring authority in view of section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act. For that reason, the process already completed had not been inadmissible.
